slots.hypothesis: Overnight vs intraday split (tug of war): ON = log(div(day_first(Open), ts_delay(day_last(Close), 1))), ID = log(div(day_last(Close), day_first(Open))). The two legs are priced by different traders. The overnight leg comes from the opening call auction, where retail and attention-driven orders cluster and buyers carry the T+1 holding constraint. The intraday leg comes from continuous trading by arbitrageurs and institutions. Which leg a stock's returns persistently fall in reflects its clientele. Implementation: ON−ID means over 20/60/120/241 days (taking the difference removes the 20-day total return used by the reversal control); single legs over windows longer than 20 days; a scale-free version that divides by mean|ON|+mean|ID|; cs_regres of ON on ID; and cross_corr / cross_regbeta of ON and ID, which are continuous versions of the Akbas daytime-reversal count (count versions fail distinct >= 0.5, and trivial booleans are avoided). Direction is set on train; the prior is -1. This is the first use of Open and of cross-day structure; all existing heads are second moments of minute returns. Literature: LPS 2019-10, Berkman et al 2012-08, Akbas et al 2022-09, Bogousslavsky 2021-07, Bai et al 2020-04, Lin-Chang-Chou 2023-06. 14 seeds.

Tradable-share supply, direction -1. Prices are back-adjusted, so sub(LogFloatCap, log(day_last(Close))) = log(shares) - log(adjustment factor) + const: price and bonus/split shares cancel exactly, cash dividends enter as -D/P, and unlocks or issuance enter as positive. Its ts_delta(.,120/241) is therefore exactly the Daniel-Titman composite issuance on the float (LogTotalCap gives the total-share version). Seeds: float and total versions over 120 and 241 days; cs_regres(float, total), which isolates the unlock component; the lock-up overhang sub(LogTotalCap, LogFloatCap) plus 241-day total issuance; 20-day means of the 241-day versions; and a 60-day float version. Mechanisms: issuance timing and payouts (DT 2006, Pontiff-Woodgate 2008), and A-share lock-up expiry supply pressure (Field-Hanka 2001, Liu-Tang 2014, Wang-Xu 2004 on free float). Risks stated up front: long-only captures only the payout leg; stocks with no corporate action form a near-zero block that is small at 241 days; the 241-day difference is missing early in train because warm-up is only 60 days; LogTotalCap includes H/B shares. 10 seeds.

Decision: both slots are N. I did not follow the analyst's suggested E + N. The direct R evaluations from r1 settled where this seed's alpha comes from. Every positive score so far comes from the convex tail of intraday realized variance, which is trap 1/3. All four de-scaled forms of the W core died (+0.18 / +0.17 / -0.71 / -0.75). The r1 E slot's best outputs all put day_var back in or re-aggregated W along the day axis. A second E on that core would only produce more volatility heads, so I am keeping its last E slot for r3. The DW(High) family is ruled out: it is realized variance and very likely has |rho| >= 0.5 with the volatility control.

Slot a (N, 14 seeds): overnight vs intraday returns. Seeds take the overnight-minus-intraday difference, which cancels the total return the 20-day reversal control already covers. Other seeds are single legs over long windows, a scale-free ratio, a cs_regres residual, and cross_corr / cross_regbeta of the two legs.

Slot b (N, 10 seeds): tradable-share supply. Because Close is back-adjusted, the difference of sub(LogFloatCap or LogTotalCap, log(day_last(Close))) is exactly Daniel-Titman composite issuance. Price and bonus shares cancel, dividends count as negative issuance, and unlocks count as positive. This replaces the analyst's raw ts_delta(LogFloatShares), which treats bonus shares (送转) as issuance and has a zero-inflation problem.

Choices made while reading the source: discrete time-position aggregators and Akbas-style counts fail the distinct >= 0.5 gate, so the seeds use continuous correlation/slope versions instead. is_gt0 and sign are marked trivial booleans in the registry, so no seed uses them. Warm-up is only 60 days, so 241-day differences lose about 180 train days, and the R variants use 120 days to stay above the 0.9 coverage gate. The label starts at the next day's 09:31-09:45 VWAP, so the next overnight move is not part of it.

R has 9 variants in 4 groups:
- head 1: x1000 rescaling to test the float32 underflow (distinct 0.55), plus a sigma^7.5 null control.
- head 4: two coefficient-of-variation versions plus a day_std(Ret) null control.
- head 8: log price as a diagnostic, plus two 120-day composite-issuance versions that could be added as new heads.
- head 2: mul replaced by div.

The notebook records my beliefs (the volatility tail is the source, 0.9), predictions (head probability 0.30 for slot a and 0.25 for slot b, plus R predictions), and a scored table of the r1 predictions with lessons learned.
